cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: Within the fused four-view patient geometry, the partition shows four sets of unequal size (13 to 39 patients) whose internal affinities are similar and whose leading spectral gaps are uniformly located at the single-cluster resolution. For every set, the eigengap at resolution 1 exceeds the next gap by two to three orders of magnitude, and screen_candidate_k is 1 throughout; this pattern describes dominance of the single-cluster resolution within each set and does not, by itself, indicate internal multi-cluster substructure. The leading-gap magnitude declines monotonically with set size, which is consistent with the smaller sets having fewer patients over which spectral structure can accumulate, rather than with a distinct internal organization. Boundary coherence is modest: the closest between-set affinities (about 0.0090 to 0.0091) sit only slightly below the within-set affinities (about 0.0094 to 0.0101), so the current memberships are not sharply separated in this geometry. K4_C0004, the smallest set, participates in three of the five closest pairs and has the highest within-set affinity, making it the most boundary-adjacent set. Taken together, the measurements indicate that the four-view geometry represents the current memberships with similar internal cohesion and without a dominant internal subdivision signal, while the boundaries between sets are relatively soft. This tool does not recluster patients, and these observations concern the coherence of the existing partition rather than any alternative partition.

The label silhouettes are near zero in CT (0.0033) and WSI (0.0031), modest in RNA (0.0634), and largest in WXS (0.0900), and the corresponding within- versus between-label mean distances are nearly indistinguishable in CT and WSI. This means that the current membership is not sharply separated from the heterogeneous rest in the imaging modalities, while RNA and WXS provide somewhat more label-aligned structure. The GRV values are low to modest (0.092 to 0.198), indicating that the four modalities share only limited global patient-geometry structure; the strongest shared structure is between WSI and RNA (GRV 0.198, permutation p 0.001) and the weakest between WSI and WXS (GRV 0.092, p 0.096). Importantly, high GRV would not by itself establish that two views support the same candidate boundary, and here the GRV values are not high; the low values can reflect complementary information across modalities rather than a faulty modality. The permutation results show that patient correspondence is more exchangeable than expected for CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA, but not for CT-RNA, CT-WXS, or WSI-WXS. Taken together, the measurements indicate that K4_C0001's current boundary is coherently represented only to a limited degree across the four views, with the strongest label alignment in WXS and RNA and the weakest in CT and WSI, and with only modest global geometry sharing among modalities. This tool does not recluster patients, so these observations describe the representation of the existing membership rather than any alternative partition.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0001, the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable with 19,449 genes and a 39-versus-64 contrast. The dominant pattern is coordinated down-regulation of a large, coherent set of pathways relative to the heterogeneous rest: oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.025, FDR 0.001), complement (NES -1.942), allograft rejection (NES -1.940), interferon alpha (NES -1.907) and gamma (NES -1.872) responses, IL6/JAK/STAT3 signaling (NES -1.830), and additional inflammatory, xenobiotic, ROS, coagulation, EMT, and metabolic pathways. The leading-edge genes for oxidative phosphorylation are overwhelmingly mitochondrial respiratory chain and TCA-cycle components, and the interferon leading edges include antigen-presentation and interferon-stimulated genes, indicating that the down-regulation is not driven by a few isolated transcripts but by broad, internally consistent programs. Up-regulated pathways are few and weaker (angiogenesis NES 1.321, FDR 0.086; UV response DN NES 1.272, FDR 0.098), so the phenotype is better characterized by loss of oxidative and immune-inflammatory programs than by a strong positive program. Because the rest group combines three other candidate sets, the contrast identifies what distinguishes K4_C0001 from that mixture rather than a clean two-group comparison; the direction and magnitude are consistent across many pathways, but the FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity corrections and do not by themselves establish biological importance.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0001 the WXS analysis is estimable across 3,583 interpretation-matrix genes with 39 target and 64 rest patients. The coherent signal is a chromatin-remodeling/VHL axis: PBRM1 is markedly enriched in the target (30/39, 77%) versus the rest (9/64, 14%), with an odds ratio of 20.4 and an interval well above one, and it is the only driver-panel gene significant under both the driver-family and global corrections (q_driver 2.6e-09, q_global 6.1e-07). VHL is also enriched (29/39 vs 27/64; OR 3.97, q_driver 0.0104) but not significant globally. In the opposite direction, BAP1 is depleted in the target (0/39 vs 13/64; OR 0.048, q_driver 0.0104), consistent with the known mutual exclusivity of PBRM1 and BAP1 in ccRCC. CDKN2A is not estimable because neither group has events. The exploratory genes with the largest nominal effects (e.g., ATM, 6/39 vs 0/64) do not survive global correction (q_global 1.0), so they are not established as phenotype-defining. Taken together, the driver-panel results describe a PBRM1-high, BAP1-low, VHL-enriched mutational profile relative to the rest of the partition, which is a recognizable ccRCC-associated pattern; the driver panel is a post-hoc annotation rather than a discovery feature set, and the rest group is a mixture of the other three sets, so the contrast is not a clean two-group comparison.

The RNA report described strong up-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation and metabolic programs, and the WXS report described a VHL-low, PBRM1-low mutational profile. The confounder results here add a complementary perspective: the significant site and acquisition associations for K4_C0002 mean that some of the structural and biological differences could be influenced by site or acquisition factors. The evidence streams are not in direct conflict, but they jointly indicate that the biological interpretation should be considered alongside the measured technical imbalance, which is more pronounced for K4_C0002 than for K4_C0001.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the fused four-view patient geometry, the partition shows four sets of unequal size (13 to 39 patients) whose internal affinities are similar and whose leading spectral gaps are uniformly located at the single-cluster resolution. For every set, the eigengap at resolution 1 exceeds the next gap by two to three orders of magnitude, and screen_candidate_k is 1 throughout; this pattern describes dominance of the single-cluster resolution within each set and does not, by itself, indicate internal multi-cluster substructure. The leading-gap magnitude declines monotonically with set size, which is consistent with the smaller sets having fewer patients over which spectral structure can accumulate, rather than with a distinct internal organization. Boundary coherence is modest: the closest between-set affinities (about 0.0090 to 0.0091) sit only slightly below the within-set affinities (about 0.0094 to 0.0101), so the current memberships are not sharply separated in this geometry. K4_C0004, the smallest set, participates in three of the five closest pairs and has the highest within-set affinity, making it the most boundary-adjacent set. Taken together, the measurements indicate that the four-view geometry represents the current memberships with similar internal cohesion and without a dominant internal subdivision signal, while the boundaries between sets are relatively soft. This tool does not recluster patients, and these observations concern the coherence of the existing partition rather than any alternative partition.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0002, the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable with 19,449 genes and a 31-versus-72 contrast. The dominant pattern is strong up-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.788, FDR 0.001), protein secretion (NES 2.273), fatty acid metabolism (NES 2.210), adipogenesis (NES 1.983), mTORC1 signaling (NES 1.942), peroxisome (NES 1.934), and additional metabolic and hormone-response programs, all with FDR at or below 0.001 for the leading pathways. The leading-edge genes for oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid metabolism are again mitochondrial respiratory chain, TCA-cycle, and lipid-oxidation genes, indicating a coherent mitochondrial/metabolic program rather than isolated gene effects. Down-regulated pathways are weaker and less coherent (myogenesis NES -1.550, FDR 0.079; Wnt NES -1.444, FDR 0.102; angiogenesis NES -1.330, FDR 0.123; allograft rejection NES -1.286, FDR 0.142; Notch NES -1.345, FDR 0.146). Because the rest group combines three other candidate sets, the contrast identifies what distinguishes K4_C0002 from that mixture; the direction and magnitude are consistent across many pathways, but FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity corrections and do not by themselves establish biological importance.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0002 the WXS analysis is estimable across 3,583 genes with 31 target and 72 rest patients. The dominant and coherent signal is depletion of the canonical ccRCC drivers: VHL is strongly depleted in the target (2/31, 6%) versus the rest (54/72, 75%), with an odds ratio of 0.023 and an interval far below one, and it is significant under both driver-family and global corrections (q_driver 9.7e-10, q_global 2.3e-07). PBRM1 is also depleted (5/31 vs 34/72; OR 0.215, q_driver 0.0273) but not significant globally. TP53 shows a nominal enrichment (3/31 vs 0/72; OR 17.8) that does not survive driver-family correction (q_driver 0.127), and KDM5C shows a weaker nominal enrichment (4/31 vs 2/72; q_driver 0.245). CDKN2A is not estimable because neither group has events. The exploratory genes with the largest nominal effects (e.g., CPEB4, 4/31 vs 0/72) do not survive global correction (q_global 1.0). Taken together, the driver-panel results describe a VHL-low, PBRM1-low mutational profile relative to the rest of the partition, which is the inverse of the K4_C0001 pattern; the driver panel is a post-hoc annotation, and the rest group is a mixture of the other three sets, so the contrast is not a clean two-group comparison.

The label silhouette is largest in WXS (0.177), modest in CT (0.053) and WSI (0.036), and near zero in RNA (0.011), and the within- versus between-label mean distances follow the same pattern, with the largest gap in WXS and the smallest in RNA. This means that the current membership is most clearly separated from the heterogeneous rest in the WXS native geometry and least clearly in RNA, while CT and WSI show intermediate, modest separation. The GRV values are low to modest (0.092 to 0.198), indicating limited global patient-geometry sharing across modalities; the strongest shared structure is between WSI and RNA (GRV 0.198, permutation p 0.001) and the weakest between WSI and WXS (GRV 0.092, p 0.096). As with K4_C0001, high GRV would not by itself establish shared boundaries, and the low values here can reflect complementary information. The permutation results show exchangeable patient correspondence for CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA, but not for CT-RNA, CT-WXS, or WSI-WXS. Taken together, the measurements indicate that K4_C0002's current boundary is coherently represented to a modest degree across the four views, with the strongest label alignment in WXS and the weakest in RNA, and with only modest global geometry sharing among modalities.
